subject: general
question: Which of the following Ministries is responsible for granting Indian citizenship by naturalisation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Home Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of granting **Indian citizenship by naturalisation** is governed under the provisions of the **Citizenship Act, 1955**.
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** is the nodal ministry responsible for implementing the Citizenship Act, 1955, and handles all matters related to citizenship, including naturalisation.
 
• Naturalisation is one of the ways to acquire Indian citizenship, which is granted to foreign nationals who meet specific eligibility criteria as outlined in the **Citizenship Act**. *Hence, the Ministry of Home Affairs is the relevant ministry for this process.*
 
• The naturalisation process involves submitting an application to the MHA, which is then scrutinised to ensure compliance with the necessary legal requirements such as residency, good character, and knowledge of an Indian language.
 
• The final decision on granting citizenship is made by the MHA after verifying the application and conducting a background check. *Thus, the Ministry of Home Affairs plays a central role in this process.*
 
• Other ministries like the **Ministry of Law and Justice**, **Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs**, or **Ministry of External Affairs** are not responsible for granting citizenship by naturalisation. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Citizenship Act, 1955:**

 
 
• The Citizenship Act, 1955 provides for the acquisition, termination, and supplementary provisions relating to Indian citizenship.
 
• It specifies five modes of acquiring Indian citizenship: **by birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, and incorporation of territory**.
 
• Naturalisation is a process where a person not born in India becomes a citizen after fulfilling certain conditions such as **12 years of residence** in India and **renunciation of foreign citizenship**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Ministry of Home Affairs:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs** ensures that applications for citizenship are processed in accordance with the law and that all necessary verifications, such as police clearance and character verification, are conducted.
 
• The MHA also coordinates with state governments and other concerned authorities for verification processes.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Citizenship by Naturalisation:**
 
 
• Applicants must have resided in India for a minimum of **12 years** (11 years preceding the application and 1 year immediately before applying).
 
• They must demonstrate **good character**, knowledge of an Indian language, and show intent to reside in India permanently.
 
• Naturalised citizens enjoy the same rights and responsibilities as citizens by birth, including voting rights and eligibility for public offices.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility for Citizenship by Naturalisation:**

 
 
• The applicant must not be an illegal migrant as per the Citizenship Act.
 
• Citizenship by naturalisation is granted only after the applicant renounces any other citizenship held previously, as India does not allow **dual citizenship**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of MHA’s Role:**
 
 
• The MHA is pivotal in ensuring that citizenship laws are implemented in a transparent and efficient manner, maintaining the sovereignty and security of India.
